question.text: Will Nueva Pescanova's octopus farm gain regulatory approval in the Canary Islands before June 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before June 1, 2027, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report that Nueva Pescanova has been officially granted regulatory approval by [the Government of the Canary Islands](https://www.gobiernodecanarias.org/principal/) to operate an octopus farm in the Canary Islands.
question.fine_print:
To qualify, the regulatory approval must be for a facility operated by Nueva Pescanova with the purpose of the production, processing, and distribution of octopuses for human consumption.

The farm does not need to be operational for this question to resolve as Yes.

research:
**Bottom line:** The question's background says there were no updates as of May 2026, but that is out of date. On 2026-07-23 Nueva Pescanova formally withdrew its application for the Las Palmas octopus farm, so there is nothing pending for the Canary Islands government to approve. A Yes would need a brand-new application that gets through environmental assessment and is approved before 2027-06-01. I found no sign that any such application exists.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria point to the Government of the Canary Islands, but it doesn't publish a dedicated status page or data series for this project. I found no notice there granting approval.
- 2023 (as reported 2026-08-04): The regional government required a full environmental impact assessment (an "Environmental Impact Declaration") for the farm. The company never submitted one. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/08/05/la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-finalmente-no-estara-en-espana-nueva-pescanova-abandona-su-polemico-proyecto-en-gran-canaria/)
- The concession itself was being processed by the Las Palmas Port Authority. That file was opened in May 2021.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-07-23: Nueva Pescanova formally told the Las Palmas Port Authority it was withdrawing its concession request. The Authority said it would archive the 2021 file. [Tercera Información](https://www.tercerainformacion.es/articulo/actualidad/24/07/2026/nueva-pescanova-retira-su-peticion-para-instalar-la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-en-canarias), [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/ngos-celebrate-as-nueva-pescanova-ditches-plans-for-octopus-farm)
- Port Authority president Beatriz Calzada said the company found it "técnicamente complicado" (technically complicated) to meet all the conditions. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/08/05/la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-finalmente-no-estara-en-espana-nueva-pescanova-abandona-su-polemico-proyecto-en-gran-canaria/)
- The company cited "business and administrative reasons". It said the withdrawal does not rule out "other solutions or locations" in future, and that it does not consider the matter closed. [Ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/naturaleza/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-a-la-granja-de-pulpos-en-canarias), [The Fish Site (FR)](https://thefishsite.com/articles/nueva-pescanova-retire-son-projet-delevage-de-poulpes-a-las-palmas)
- I could not confirm that the file has actually been formally archived. I also found no new Nueva Pescanova application in the Canary Islands.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-11: The news-API articles provided (on the Canary Islands' 2027 budget and similar topics) don't mention the octopus farm.
- 2026-08-30: Canarias7, citing unnamed sources, reports that the real reason was poor survival in captivity. Projected output had fallen from 3,000 to about 15-30 tonnes a year. I could not verify this independently. [Canarias7](https://www.canarias7.es/economia/3000-toneladas-baja-produccion-mato-granja-pulpos-20260830071226-nt.html)
- 2026-08-04: Infobae summary:
  - The dumping (water discharge) authorization procedure was declared expired in January 2026.
  - In May 2026 the Port Authority started proceedings to expire the whole file.
  - Campaigners sent more than 43,000 emails asking for it to be archived.
  [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/08/05/la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-finalmente-no-estara-en-espana-nueva-pescanova-abandona-su-polemico-proyecto-en-gran-canaria/)
- 2026-07-24: The animal-rights party PACMA celebrated the "definitive shelving" of the project. [PACMA](https://pacma.es/notas-de-prensa/pacma-celebra-el-carpetazo-definitivo-al-proyecto-de-granja-de-pulpos-de-nueva-pescanova-en-gran-canaria/)
- AnimaNaturalis warns that without a national ban another company could revive the idea. It also notes that the Xunta de Galicia (the Galician regional government) has licensed similar projects. Those are outside the Canary Islands, so they wouldn't count for this question. [Democrata](https://www.democrata.es/economia/animanaturalis-celebra-el-fin-de-la-granja-de-pulpos-en-canarias-y-reclama-vetarla-en-toda-espana/)

## 4. Base rates
- In about 5 years (May 2021 to July 2026) the project never got approval. It failed the simplified environmental assessment, the regional government demanded a full assessment, and the discharge permit lapsed in January 2026.
- I know of no case where a project withdrawn like this was re-filed and approved within about 10 months. A full environmental impact assessment in Spain usually takes well over a year, but that is my own general estimate, not a sourced figure.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question.
- None of the collected markets match it. The closest is only loosely related: Kalshi's 2027 Canary Islands regional election winner market (PSOE 0.55, CC 0.33, PP 0.11).

## 6. Upcoming events that could move the outcome
- The Port Authority formally archiving the 2021 file. This would confirm the current state but not change it.
- Any new Nueva Pescanova filing in the Canary Islands. I found no sign of one.
- Spain's bill to ban octopus aquaculture, filed by Sumar and others and admitted for processing on 2025-06-17:
  - The Republican group withdrew its signature in September 2025.
  - It is still waiting for a plenary vote.
  - If passed, it would make approval legally impossible.
  [BOCG](https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/B/BOCG-15-B-241-1.PDF), [Ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/?p=496446)
- The Spanish general election on 2026-11-29, according to the news-API items, and the 2027 Canary regional election. Either could change the political climate for the ban bill or for aquaculture permitting.

[PACMA](https://pacma.es/notas-de-prensa/pacma-celebra-el-carpetazo-definitivo-al-proyecto-de-granja-de-pulpos-de-nueva-pescanova-en-gran-canaria/); [Euro Weekly News](https://euroweeklynews.com/2026/07/24/worlds-first-octopus-farm-left-dead-in-the-water-in-spain/); [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/ngos-celebrate-as-nueva-pescanova-ditches-plans-for-octopus-farm) (403 when fetched, headline only)

- I found no news from September to November 2026 about a new Nueva Pescanova octopus project. The news-API items you supplied (Canary 2027 budget, Mogán politics and others) are unrelated.

## 4. Base rates
- No government anywhere has approved a commercial octopus farm. Infobae notes the Xunta de Galicia has licensed "similar projects", but gives no details and I could not verify this.
- This project made no regulatory progress in about 5 years (2021 to 2026): the environmental report was rejected, the DIA was never filed, and the permits expired.
- A new aquaculture environmental assessment and port concession in Spain usually takes years, not months.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires:** About 6.5 months remain until the 2027-06-01 deadline. Yes requires credible reports that the Government of the Canary Islands officially granted Nueva Pescanova regulatory approval for an octopus farm for human consumption in the Canaries.

**(b) Status quo:** No. On 2026-07-23 Nueva Pescanova formally withdrew its Las Palmas port concession application, and the 2021 file is being archived. Nothing is pending that could be approved.

**(c) Base rate:** No government anywhere has approved a commercial octopus farm. This project made no regulatory progress in about 5 years. A full Spanish environmental impact assessment plus a port concession usually takes well over a year. The chance that a withdrawn aquaculture project is re-filed and fully approved within roughly 10 months is close to 0%, under 1%.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **For Yes:**
  - The company said in July and August 2026 that it does not consider the matter closed and may look at "other solutions or locations."
- **For No:**
  - Formal withdrawal on 2026-07-23.
  - The discharge permit procedure expired in January 2026.
  - The Port Authority started expiry proceedings in May 2026.
  - The full environmental assessment (DIA) required since 2023 was never submitted.
  - Canarias7 reported on 2026-08-30 that captive survival was poor, with projected output down to 15-30 tonnes a year from 3,000.
  - No new filing had been reported as of November 2026.
  - Strong NGO opposition continues, and a national ban bill is pending.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** The company focuses elsewhere (for example Galicia) or shelves octopus farming, and no Canary application is approved before June 2027. This is very likely.
- **Yes:** The company quietly files a redesigned project at a new Canary site in late 2026. It obtains a favourable environmental declaration and approval by May 2027 despite the timelines. This is nearly implausible given the procedures and the company's stated technical difficulties.

**(f) From base rate to final probability:** I start near 0.5% because nothing is pending and no new application exists. I nudge up slightly for unknowns, such as possible misreporting or a quiet new filing, and to protect against the log-score penalty. The research shows the outcome is effectively decided, so a sub-3% figure is justified.

Probability: 1%

(b) The status quo is No. On 2026-07-23 Nueva Pescanova formally withdrew its only application, the Las Palmas Port Authority concession, and the file is being archived. Nothing is pending for the government to approve.
